title: SQL Set 04: University Courses, Prerequisites & Grading
description: Division queries, top scorers per course, pass percentage calculations, and orphan enrollment checks.

queries.title: Students Enrolled in ALL Core Courses
queries.prompt: Find `student_id` and `student_name` of students enrolled in every course present in `core_courses`, ordered by `student_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE students (student_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_name TEXT); CREATE TABLE core_courses (course_code TEXT PRIMARY KEY); CREATE TABLE enrollments (student_id INT, course_code TEXT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO students VALUES (1,'Aditi'),(2,'Bhavesh'),(3,'Charu'); INSERT INTO core_courses VALUES ('CS101'),('CS102'),('CS103'); INSERT INTO enrollments VALUES (1,'CS101'),(1,'CS102'),(1,'CS103'),(1,'EL201'),(2,'CS101'),(2,'CS102'),(3,'CS101'),(3,'CS102'),(3,'CS103');
queries.solutionSql: SELECT s.student_id, s.student_name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id JOIN core_courses c ON e.course_code = c.course_code GROUP BY s.student_id, s.student_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.course_code) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM core_courses) ORDER BY s.student_id;
queries.explanation: Inner-joining `core_courses` ignores electives (`EL201`), then `HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.course_code) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM core_courses)` performs exact relational division.

queries.title: Top 2 Scores Per Course
queries.prompt: Return `course_id`, `student_name`, and `marks` for the top 2 students in each course (break ties by `student_name` ascending). Order by `course_id` ascending, `marks` descending, `student_name` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE grades (course_id TEXT, student_name TEXT, marks INT);
queries.solutionSql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT course_id, student_name, marks, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY marks DESC, student_name ASC) AS rn FROM grades) SELECT course_id, student_name, marks FROM ranked WHERE rn <= 2 ORDER BY course_id ASC, marks DESC, student_name ASC;
queries.explanation: `ROW_NUMBER()` with `(marks DESC, student_name ASC)` deterministically caps each partition to 2 rows.

queries.title: Course Pass Percentage (Marks >= 40)
queries.prompt: For each `course_code` in `exam_results`, compute `pass_pct` rounded to 2 decimal places (`ROUND(100.0 * pass_count / total, 2)`). Order by `course_code` ascending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE exam_results (roll_no INT, course_code TEXT, marks INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT course_code, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN marks >= 40 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_pct FROM exam_results GROUP BY course_code ORDER BY course_code;
queries.explanation: Multiplying by `100.0` (floating point) avoids SQLite integer division truncation before `ROUND(..., 2)`.

queries.title: Faculty Without Assigned Sections
queries.prompt: Return `prof_id` and `prof_name` of faculty members who have zero assigned rows in `sections`, ordered by `prof_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE faculty (prof_id INT PRIMARY KEY, prof_name TEXT); CREATE TABLE sections (sec_id INT PRIMARY KEY, prof_id INT);
queries.seedSql: INSERT INTO faculty VALUES (1,'Dr. Rao'),(2,'Dr. Iyer'),(3,'Dr. Bose'); INSERT INTO sections VALUES (10,1),(11,3);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT f.prof_id, f.prof_name FROM faculty f LEFT JOIN sections s ON f.prof_id = s.prof_id WHERE s.sec_id IS NULL ORDER BY f.prof_id;
queries.explanation: Filtering `WHERE s.sec_id IS NULL` after a `LEFT JOIN` yields unmatched parent records.

queries.title: Compare Submitted Scores vs All-Student Average
queries.prompt: Compute `submitted_count` (non-NULL scores), `total_students`, and `avg_submitted` rounded to 1 decimal place per `quiz_id` in `quiz_scores`. Order by `quiz_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE quiz_scores (quiz_id INT, student_id INT, score INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT quiz_id, COUNT(score) AS submitted_count, COUNT(*) AS total_students, ROUND(AVG(score), 1) AS avg_submitted FROM quiz_scores GROUP BY quiz_id ORDER BY quiz_id;
queries.explanation: `COUNT(score)` and `AVG(score)` automatically skip NULLs, whereas `COUNT(*)` counts every row including absent submissions.
